facts.text: Trailing-twelve-month revenue is ₹38,633 cr, +12% on the prior twelve months.
Trailing-twelve-month PAT is ₹4,903 cr, +24% on the prior twelve months.
Sep 2026 quarter: revenue ₹9,977 cr (+17% YoY), PAT ₹1,085 cr (+7% YoY), operating margin 15.6%.
Revenue has compounded at 10% over 10 years, 10% over 5 and 1% over 3; the last twelve months (+12%) are running ahead of the 3-year pace.
Profit and revenue have compounded at a similar pace over 3 years (2% vs 1%).
Quarterly revenue growth has accelerated over the last four quarters: +4% → +11% → +18% → +17% YoY.
Operating margin has compressed to 15.6% from 17.6% a year ago (−2.0 pp).
Annual operating margin has ranged from 16% to 21% over five years; the latest year (19%) sits inside that range.
Borrowings are ₹4,596 cr against equity of ₹21,735 cr: debt/equity 0.21× (was 0.12× in Mar 2023).
Operating profit plus other income covers interest 38.7× over the last twelve months.
The cash conversion cycle has shortened to 84 days from 99 in Mar 2023 (payable days 71 → 79).
Promoters hold 52.6%, unchanged over a year.
Foreign institutions hold 13.8%, +2.1 pp over a year.
Over 5 years, ₹22,795 cr of operating cash came from ₹31,355 cr of operating profit: 73% conversion; against PAT of ₹20,943 cr that is 1.1×.
Free cash flow was negative in 0 of the last 5 years; cumulative ₹15,070 cr, latest year ₹5,604 cr.
Capex ran at 4% of revenue in Mar 2026, about ₹1,484 cr (averaged 6% over the three years before).

business.what: Asian Paints is a multinational company primarily engaged in the manufacturing and selling of paints, coatings, home décor products, modular kitchens, wardrobes, bath fittings, and sanitaryware. It generates revenue through the sale of these products across retail and project markets globally.

segments.note: Operations across 13 countries in four key regions.

claims.claim: Decorative volume growth was 6.4% in Q2, while value growth was 14.5%.
claims.quote: we have been able to grow at a good volume of about 6.4% at the base of the last year... the value growth has also been very strong at 14.5%.

claims.claim: Gross margin dipped in Q2 despite price increases due to higher inflation.
claims.quote: from a higher gross margin of where we have been from 45%, 44%, this quarter we have seen a little bit of a dip

claims.claim: The VAE facility was commissioned in September in record time.
claims.quote: I'm proud to announce that in September we started our VAE facility and this is something which has been implemented in a record time

claims.claim: New products contribute to about 18% of the revenues.
claims.quote: today I'm happy to announce that we keep on testing this benchmark of the new product contribution to the overall revenues and today the new products contribute to about 18% of the revenues

claims.claim: The company likely grew slightly higher than the industry average during the quarter.
claims.quote: what we see is that possibly we would have grown slightly higher than the industry average.

claims.claim: Rural market growth has been significantly better than urban market growth, a trend continuing from Q4.
claims.quote: We have seen that growth in rural markets has been much better compared to urban markets. This was a trend that we also saw in Q4, and trend continues to strengthen.

claims.claim: The company expects to reach a VAE capacity of 150,000 MT over a period of 2 to 2.5 years.
claims.quote: Our feeling is that possibly over a period of about 2-2.5 years, we should be able to reach basically a capacity which is higher and closer to about 150,000 MT.

claims.claim: The weighted average price increase implemented during the quarter was approximately 7%.
claims.quote: the overall weighted average price increase was around 7%.

claims.claim: Gross margins reached an all-time high of 45.6% in Q4 due to market deflation.
claims.quote: taking our Gross Margins to almost an all- time high of about 45.6%, which is very strong.

claims.claim: The company has taken cumulative price increases of 10.5-11% to combat inflation.
claims.quote: despite very strong inflation, where we have already taken close to about 10.5 - 11% price increase

claims.claim: Competitive intensity remains high with no let-up in discounting across retailers and contractors.
claims.quote: we have not seen any let -up in terms of the discounting in the market.

claims.claim: The VAM-VAE backward integration project is expected to commission its first phase in the first half of this year.
claims.quote: we expect to commission first phase in the first half of this year.

claims.claim: The company achieved an all-time high PBT margin in the PPGAP JV, up 300 bps year-on-year.
claims.quote: It is an all-time high with almost 300 bps growth year on year.

claims.claim: The company is leading the market in share of voice across all regions in India.
claims.quote: Possibly from a share of voice point of view, we are leading the game today not only in terms of north, east, west markets but also across the southern markets.

claims.claim: The company observed that rural markets performed better than urban centers in Q3.
claims.quote: One of the things which we saw was, that the rural parts batted better than the urban centres, possibly a good rainfall which has augured well.

claims.claim: Recent price increases by competitors are artificial and lack meaning as they do not impact the market.
claims.quote: So as per us, possibly this price increase has no meaning, because anything which is in the zone of about 2 to 3% will not have any impact.

claims.claim: Asian Paints claims to be the number one integrated home decor player.
claims.quote: today we claim to be the number one integrated home decor player.

claims.claim: New products contribute more than 15% of the company's revenue.
claims.quote: new products contribute more than 15% of our revenue.

claims.claim: Gross margins expanded by 270 bps year-on-year in Q2 FY26.
claims.quote: Gross margins have expanded by 270bps to 43.7%. At the same time, we are up 270 bps from same quarter last year.

claims.claim: The overall industry growth in Q2 was only 3.5-4%.
claims.quote: The industry, in the Q2 has just grown by about 3.5-4%.

claims.claim: We are seeing a slight uptick in demand sequentially in both T1, T2 cities and T3, T4 cities.
claims.quote: we saw a slight uptick in demand sequentially and both T1, T2 cities and T3, T4 cities, we were seeing almost equal demand conditions.

claims.claim: The anti-dumping duty on TiO2 will have an impact of 1.5% to 2.5% on the overall raw material cost index.
claims.quote: From the point of impact of ADD alone, the impact would be anywhere from 1.5% to 2.5% in the overall raw material cost index level.

claims.claim: The 10% extra grammage offered by new competition is viewed as a discount rather than a consumer proposition.
claims.quote: I think that according to us will not really matter too much in this thing you have seen almost a year plus, that thing going in the market, and we see it as a discount

claims.claim: Gross margins have been consistent in the band of 43% to 43.5% over several quarters.
claims.quote: Overall we have seen gross margins largely consistent in the band of about that 43 to 43.5% kind of a zone and that has been consistent over the several quarters.

pressure.question: Do you see any risk to that 18% to 20% band at the EBITDA margin level?
Is the industry able to pass on all the increases or is it still some time away?
Can you break down the 7% volume-value gap into pure price increase and mix change?
At what crude level does the 18-20% margin equation set in?
Can you maintain 18-20% margins if crude stays in the $90-$100 band?
Does competitive intensity imply discounting will remain high?
Why is industry growth muted despite your activities and increased media spend?
Will the volume-value gap become zero or remain at 3-4%?
Can you sustain double-digit volume growth in coming quarters?
Is competitive intensity waning from a dealer adoption point of view?
Do you see reversing of green shoots due to job cuts and how is new competition performing?
Is the QoQ gross margin erosion a reflection of high rebating in the industry?

synthesis.one_liner: Asian Paints accelerated revenue growth to 12% TTM, but operating margins compressed to 15.6% as inflation offset price increases.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management maintains its operating margin target of 18% to 20% for the full year.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Operating margin compressed to 15.6% in the Sep 2026 quarter, missing the guided band.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management guides for a full-year volume growth band of 8% to 9%.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Decorative volume growth was 6.4% in the Q2 FY27 quarter, running below the guided pace.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management guided for a capex commitment of 700 crores for the fiscal year.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Actual capex ran at ₹1,484 cr in Mar 2026, more than double the guided amount.

synthesis.credibility: The ledger shows zero delivered items out of 16 tracked guidance points, with one explicit miss in capex where actual spending doubled guidance. Margin targets are currently breached by reported quarterly results.

bull.evidence: Quarterly revenue growth accelerated over the last four quarters from 4% to 17% YoY.
Free cash flow was positive in all of the last 5 years, reaching ₹5,604 cr in the latest year.
Borrowings stand at ₹4,596 cr against equity of ₹21,735 cr, representing a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21x.

bear.evidence: Operating margin compressed to 15.6% in the Sep 2026 quarter, down 2.0 pp from 17.6% a year ago.
Actual capex reached ₹1,484 cr in Mar 2026, significantly exceeding the initial ₹700 cr guidance.
Three-year revenue compound growth rate has slowed to 1%, lagging the 10% ten-year historical rate.

watch: Operating margin recovery back into the 18-20% guided band
Quarterly volume growth trajectory relative to the 8-9% target
